security.title: Security Architecture
security.subtitle: Defence in depth, zero trust, encryption first — our security architecture protects your data at every layer.
security.zeroTrustDesc: Autional follows a zero-trust security model built on "never trust, always verify". Every access request, from inside or outside the network, is subject to authentication and authorisation checks.
security.encryption: Encryption in Transit and at Rest
security.encryptionDesc: Data is encrypted both in transit and at rest.
security.infrastructureDesc: Containerised cloud infrastructure combined with defence-in-depth, delivering a stable, rollback-capable runtime environment.
security.observabilityDesc: Full traceability of all operations with tamper-proof audit logs, providing complete evidence chains for security incident investigations and compliance audits.
security.bugBountyDesc: We welcome vulnerability reports from security researchers through public channels, and track and acknowledge valid reports.
security.codeAuditDesc: Code changes are merged after passing CI pipeline checks, with continuous dependency vulnerability scanning.
security.soc247Desc: We continuously monitor system health and security events through centralised log collection and alerting.
security.vulnerabilityDisclosureDesc: We welcome responsible disclosure. Please reach us through the channels listed in our vulnerability disclosure policy.
security.items.zeroTrust: Principle of least privilege (PoLP) — deny by default
Multi-tenant isolation — strict separation of tenant data and permissions
Role-based access control (RBAC) with fine-grained permission checks
Session management — revocation, timeout and risk controls
security.items.encryption: Transport encryption: HTTPS/TLS across all paths
Key management: centralised key management service with rotation
Secrets held centrally, never hard-coded in application code
security.items.infrastructure: Containerised deployment with unified CI builds and versioned artifacts
Service health checks and automated rollback
Cloud network isolation with minimal open ports
security.items.observability: Audit log hash chain verification, preventing after-the-fact tampering
Centralised log collection and alerting (Loki / Alertmanager)
Audit anomaly detection with automated alerting

privacy.title: Privacy Policy
privacy.subtitle: Your privacy is important to us. This policy explains how we collect, use, and protect your personal information.
privacy.contactDpoDesc: If you have any questions about our privacy policy or wish to exercise your data subject rights, please contact our DPO:
privacy.dpoAddressText: Autional Data Protection Office, Shenzhen, China
privacy.sections.collection: Account information: username, email, phone number, password hash (irreversibly encrypted storage).
Usage data: login time, IP address, device fingerprint, operation logs (for security auditing and anomaly detection).
Tenant configuration: company name, department structure, application configuration, branding customization information.
Payment information: billing address, transaction records (card numbers are processed by third-party payment gateways; Autional does not store full card numbers).
privacy.sections.usage: Providing identity authentication and access management services.
Ensuring account security and fraud detection.
Fulfilling legal and compliance obligations (e.g., tax, audit).
With your explicit consent, sending product updates and security notifications.
privacy.sections.sharing: We never sell your personal data to third parties.

Data is shared only under the following circumstances: (a) with your explicit authorization; (b) with partners necessary for service delivery (e.g., cloud infrastructure providers); (c) as required by law or regulation.
All third-party subprocessors are bound by Data Processing Agreements (DPA) and meet equivalent security standards.
privacy.sections.crossBorder: By default, data is stored in the geographic region of your choice (see Data Residency page).
When cross-border data transfer is required, we use EU Commission-approved Standard Contractual Clauses (SCC) or other legal mechanisms.
You can always learn about your data storage location and cross-border transfer status.
privacy.sections.retention: Account data is retained until you delete your account or 90 days after contract termination, unless a longer period is required by law.
Audit logs are retained as required by applicable regulations.
You may request deletion of your personal data at any time (GDPR right to erasure / China Personal Information Protection Law).
privacy.sections.rights: Right of access: understand what data we hold about you.
Right of rectification: update inaccurate or incomplete personal data.
Right of erasure: request deletion of your personal data.
Right of portability: obtain a copy of your personal data in a structured, commonly used format.
Right to object: object to processing based on legitimate interests.
Right to withdraw consent: withdraw previously given consent at any time.
privacy.sections.cookies: We use essential cookies to maintain service operations (e.g., session persistence, security tokens).
Analytics cookies are used solely to improve product experience and are not used for cross-site tracking.
You can manage cookie preferences through browser settings, but disabling essential cookies may affect service usage.
privacy.device.title: Device Data Privacy
privacy.device.subtitle: What the Autional Authenticator processes on your devices — and how we protect it.
privacy.device.meta: How the Autional Authenticator handles device data — what we process, why, how it is encrypted, and your controls.
privacy.device.sections.collection: Push subscriptions (for login-approval push): the push service endpoint address, push encryption keys generated by your browser, a device name and type, and the browser identifier (User-Agent).

Device sync (for cross-device TOTP sync): a generic device name inferred from the browser identifier (e.g. iPhone, Android, Windows PC), a device fingerprint (a one-way SHA-256 hash derived from the browser identifier, language, screen parameters and similar values — the raw values are never uploaded), and the synced TOTP account data (account name, username, TOTP secret and algorithm parameters).
Cloud backup (for backup & restore): only the backup ciphertext encrypted on your device, together with its checksum and basic metadata (account count, version, device name).
Login-approval records (for your own security review): the status, time and context of push approval challenges.
privacy.device.sections.usage: To deliver login-approval requests to your devices (push MFA) and protect your account;
To sync your TOTP accounts across your devices and support switching to a new device;
To back up and restore your TOTP accounts;
To show you your own login-approval activity.
None of this data is used for advertising or cross-site tracking.
privacy.device.sections.storage: All transmission is encrypted over HTTPS/TLS;
Device-sync data is encrypted at rest on our servers; to sync it across your devices, the server must be able to decrypt it before delivering it to a device you own;
Cloud backups are encrypted on your device first (AES-GCM; the key stays on your device and can be protected with a PIN) — the server stores only ciphertext and cannot decrypt its contents;
Device fingerprints are one-way hashes and cannot be reversed into the original device parameters.
privacy.device.sections.controls: Push subscriptions: revoke any device on the Devices page — revoking deletes the subscription and stops pushes immediately;
Device sync: unbind a device on the Device Sync page — unbinding deletes that device's synced data (a limit on the number of synced devices applies);
Cloud backup: uploading a new backup keeps up to 3 versions and automatically evicts the oldest (to delete cloud backup data, contact privacy@autional.net);
Login-approval records are visible only to you.
privacy.device.sections.retention: The data above is retained until you delete it (revoke / unbind / delete backup), or handled under the retention and deletion terms of our Privacy Policy when your account is closed.

vdp.title: Vulnerability Disclosure Policy
vdp.subtitle: We value the contributions of the security research community and welcome responsible disclosure of security vulnerabilities. This policy defines the scope, rules, and process.
vdp.scope.title: Scope
vdp.scope.desc: The following systems and assets are in scope. Testing outside this scope requires prior written authorization.

vdp.rules.title: Rules of Engagement
vdp.rules.desc: To protect user data and service stability, please follow these testing rules.
vdp.rules.items: No automated scanning that generates excessive traffic
No accessing or modifying other users' data
No lateral movement or persistence using vulnerabilities
Please use only your own test accounts
Stop immediately upon discovering a vulnerability and report it
Provide reproducible PoC and impact assessment
Do not publicly disclose before the vulnerability is fixed
vdp.report.title: How to Report
vdp.report.desc: Please report security vulnerabilities through the following channels. We recommend using PGP encryption.
vdp.report.emailDesc: Reports should include: vulnerability description, affected endpoints/components, reproduction steps, impact assessment, and remediation suggestions.
vdp.report.pgpNotice: The PGP public key has not been published yet. For encrypted communication, email security@autional.net to get the current public key and fingerprint.

vdp.safeHarbor.title: Safe Harbor
vdp.safeHarbor.commitment: Autional commits to not pursuing legal action against good-faith security research that faithfully follows this policy. We recognize and appreciate the efforts of the security community in protecting our mutual users.
vdp.safeHarbor.conditions: Safe harbor protection is contingent on: obtaining explicit authorization before exceeding the scope defined in this policy; not causing actual damage or data breach; destroying all Autional data obtained during testing after reporting.

vdp.hallOfFame.desc: We will soon launch a Security Researcher Hall of Fame to recognize outstanding contributions from the security research community. Thank you to every researcher working to protect user security!
